title: Topic
description: A topic is a self-contained map: a framework, a set of principles, and results relating them.

require_sources.description: Reject result/model records without a nonempty source. Opt in for existing datasets; enabled for new topics.

source_catalog.description: Direct sources used to classify and filter results and models. Miscellaneous records use the reserved id misc.

principle_categories.description: Ordered display categories for the principle filter. Principles refer to these ids via category.

hidden_by_default.description: Start this category hidden in the graph and conjecture lists; readers can show it with the usual controls.

framework.description: The setting all principles are stated in: the objects, the primitive relation(s), standing conventions. Every result is a claim about this framework.

background.description: Principle ids assumed throughout. Every implication and independence is read relative to these.

background_presets.description: Named, removable viewer assumption packages and abbreviations for equivalent conjunctions. Defaults apply only when the URL has no explicit assume parameter. Abbreviations do not change stored premises or model assertions.

views.description: Curated graph views, offered in the graph's View menu. A view sets exactly which principles the graph shows; it does not change the background.

default.description: Open the graph on this view when the URL names none.

principles.description: Exactly the principles the view shows.

lattice_views.description: Curated lattice views, offered in the lattice's View menu, independent of the graph views. A view sets exactly which principles the lattice draws; it does not change the background.

default.description: Open the lattice on this view when the URL names none.

principles.description: Exactly the principles the view shows. Keep it small: the lattice draws every conjunction.

notation.description: Optional notation guide shown in the viewer.

lean_lib.description: Lake library name under topics/<topic>/lean/, e.g. UnboundedUtility.

lean.description: How this topic writes a generated Lean statement; {def} stands for a principle's lean_def. Without it, principles are plain propositions and a result reads A → B → C.

namespace.description: Namespace the definitions live in. Default: the prefix of the first lean_def.

definition_check.description: Template checking that a lean_def elaborates, may span lines. Default: example : Prop := {def}

binder.description: Line after `def name : Prop :=`, e.g. a ∀ or ∃ with its variables; empty for none.

principle.description: How a principle applies inside the statement; {def} is its lean_def. Default {def}.

falsum.description: How a result concluding False is written. Default: False.

binder.description: Line after `def name : Prop :=`, e.g. a ∀ or ∃ with its variables; empty for none.

principle.description: How a principle applies inside the statement; {def} is its lean_def. Default {def}.

script.description: Lean file, relative to the topic's lean directory, that lean-check runs with `lake env lean` after a successful build to write the index.

file.description: The index it writes, relative to the topic's lean directory: for each certificate and variant, where its proofs and definitions are.

index.description: The index of source locations the viewer links each result, principle and variant to.

source_url.description: Template for a link to a source location: {commit}, {file} (relative to the topic's lean directory), {start} and {end} lines. The build fills {commit} with the commit it was built from.

draft.description: A draft topic: built and validated, but its rankings, settled share and recorded-conjecture list are not computed, and commands skip it unless it is named.
